headline: Government: Without the Maximum Price System, September Inflation Would Have Been 3.5% - Suppressed by 0.6 Percentage Points
summary: The government estimated that without the petroleum product maximum price system, September consumer inflation would have been 3.5%. The actual reading was 2.9%, 0.6 percentage points lower.
why: Consumer price inflation drives central bank policy and interest rate expectations. Fuel prices are a major component of headline inflation in most economies.
